newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan NCB says MOF carrying out routine inspection.
newsitem.headline: Japan NCB says MOF carrying out routine inspection.

text.p: Japan's Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) said the Ministry of Finance (MOF) began an inspection of its operations on Wednesday.

The inspection was not a surprise, as the long-term credit bank said earlier this week that it was preparing for a regular inspection by the ministry. The ministry's last inspection of NCB was conducted in August 1993.
An NCB official told Reuters on Wednesday that the ministry had started the inspection earlier in the morning.
Japanese newspapers reported last weekend that MOF would conduct an inspection this week to clarify the position regarding of the bank's assets and problem loans.
The inspection will help NCB win agreement from financial firms which have been asked to buy new shares it will issue to boost its capital, the newspapers said.

On April 1, NCB unveiled a restructuring plan, supported by MOF, under which it said it would aggressively write off problem loans and retreat from overseas operations. It also said it was selling prime real estate and floating new shares to try to rebuild its capital base.

NCB announced last week that it intends to increase its capital by 290.7 billion yen by issuing ordinary and preferred shares, but financial sources said private-sector financial institutions have been reluctant to buy.
